newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end down but off lows on Ramos news.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end down but off lows on Ramos news.

text.p: Manila shares plunged at the open on Monday on news that President Fidel Ramos had undergone surgery but recovered somewhat by the close, brokers said.
The Philippine composite Index closed down 40.28 points, or 1.27 percent, at 3,139.92 points, off a low of 3,112.56.
"The market over-reacted on news of the surgery but rebounded a little bit in midsession on news that it was successful," said Felix Barrientos, a trader at ING Barings Securities.

"In markets like the Philippines where the chief executive officer is seen as a very strong and powerful leader, the market is very sensitive on news about his health. There was a lot of foreign selling," said Raul Ruiz, vice president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.

President Ramos underwent surgery on Monday to remove a significant blockage in one of his arteries. The Makati Medical Centre said the president was recovering and was likely to check out on Christmas Day or the day after.
Also affecting the market was a steep fall in heavweight telecommunications firm PLDT.
